capabilities: score each note's staleness from edit, open, and inbound-link recency
work through a ranked review queue with snoozing
dim stale notes in the file explorer and show scores in the status bar
set per-note decay half-lives via a frontmatter key
export all decay scores as CSV
extras: Freemium: the free tier covers scoring and the queue; Pro ($29 one-time, shared across the author's five Second Read add-ons) adds topic grouping and superseded-note detection. Both Pro features are currently switched off because the local semantic engine has no published build yet. The plugin logs which notes you open to a local file and discloses this; Pro engine features are desktop-only.
motivation: The author notes that every vault accumulates notes that were true when written and are not now, and nothing tells you which ones.
problem: Vaults accumulate outdated notes with no signal of which ones are stale, and Obsidian does not even record when a note was last opened.

relations.evidence: Effort Index writes editing time into the same log

requires.name: Second Read Pro license ($29 one-time) for topic grouping and superseded-note detection

summary: Note-staleness scorer that ranks every note by edit, open, and inbound-link recency into a decay-ranked review queue.
